analysis.title: Flows & Liquidity: Bottoming out?
key_insights: JPM's overall equity positioning metric is significantly lower than the mid-September peak. Some near-term headwinds from last week remain, but positioning adjustments could start to limit downside.

Funding concerns around neoclouds (AI compute rental providers) took center stage over the past week. Credit research expects publicly listed neoclouds to shift toward equity financing and project-specific debt as high yield funding costs rise.
Equity research notes that a higher cost of capital could limit return headroom for neoclouds, but strong compute demand may allow some cost pass-through to customers (CoreWeave note, Oct 16).

JPM does not expect the AI capex cycle to be derailed even if the neocloud funding model becomes unviable. Publicly listed neoclouds are a small segment: about $30bn of the roughly $2.2tr of tech operating cash flows and about $80bn of the roughly $1.8tr of tech capex projected for this year.
Other tech companies with stronger balance sheets, such as hyperscalers, could absorb the neoclouds' AI infrastructure build-out.

The tech sector as a whole runs a financing surplus of about $400bn in 2026 because cash flows exceed capex, so it does not need external financing in aggregate. A scenario with capex growing 25% a year and cash flows 20% a year to 2030 still leaves a slight surplus.

Tech sector debt issuance is driven mainly by the wish to maintain buybacks while capex rises. If funding stress spreads, tech firms could postpone buybacks and use circular financing, with surplus firms such as chip makers funding deficit firms such as neoclouds.
AI capex and cash flow are underpinned by large-enterprise AI spending, which surveys suggest could reach $1.5tr globally this year.

Since Q2 2026 JPM sees semiconductor VaR shocks becoming more frequent even if AI fundamentals stay robust. Semiconductors have a large and rising share of equity markets, and VaR-based risk budgets force position cuts when volatility rises, which can cause self-reinforcing selling.

Information technology is about 40% of MSCI ACWI risk capital against a 28% market cap weight. Semiconductors are about 21% of risk capital against a 13% market cap weight, roughly a fifth of global equity risk capital.

HFRX Equity Hedge has closely tracked SMH since late September, as it did from early April to late July. In corrections this co-movement can signal forced de-risking. JPM suspects the elevated long semiconductor exposure of hedge funds and CTAs has largely unwound.

Little sign of diversification out of US assets at the aggregate level. Foreign net purchases of US equities average about $75bn a month in 2026 and bonds just under $85bn a month, above 2025 averages of just over $60bn and just under $75bn. July combined purchases were $40bn, the weakest since April 2025, and August rebounded to about $300bn.
Euro area and Japanese assets also kept strong foreign inflows YTD. Euro area bond inflows are stronger YTD than for all of 2025, though French spreads to Bunds began widening in September.
FX reserve managers show the clearest diversification: the dollar share of reserves has declined, a long-standing trend, with gold the main beneficiary.

Danish and Finnish pension funds reversed their earlier rise in USD hedge ratios this year, and Australian super fund hedge ratios are little changed. Cross-currency basis and flows into currency-hedged US ETFs show only a modest inclination to hedge dollar exposure.
The Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act on September 15. Passage this year now looks unlikely, with hopes shifting to 2027, yet crypto sentiment has stayed relatively constructive.

Regulators are working around the legislative gap. The SEC is developing a proposed five-year Innovation Exemption for tokenized equities that could trade longer hours or 24/7 with faster settlement. Scope is narrow, excludes synthetic tokens, and issuers can opt out.

More issuers opting out of tokenization dented sentiment for application tokens such as ethereum, with ETH ETF outflows and a weaker ETH futures position proxy, in contrast to the period right after the September 15 SEC announcement.

The CFTC is exploring a new market category for leveraged retail crypto trading on compliant US platforms. It is early stage, a request for feedback, with meaningful implementation unlikely before 2027.

Stablecoins are the most durable regulatory segment, supported by the GENIUS Act. The OCC has granted national trust charters to a growing set of issuers, though ICBA has sued the OCC over aspects of the approvals. FASB is considering letting corporates classify qualifying stablecoins as cash equivalents, with comments open until November 19.

JPM expects elevated political and legal risk premia in crypto until comprehensive market-structure legislation passes. The current regulatory patchwork could be overturned within two years if a Democrat wins the White House.

Appendix volatility monitor: 3-month implied vol for the S&P 500 is 15%, 1.55x realized. Brent implied vol is 46% and 10y US swaption vol is 100bp, near its Oct 5 high of 108. CDX IG and HY implied vol are 2.15x and 2.07x realized.
Bitcoin market price is $83k against an estimated production cost of $88k.

sector_views.rationale: Fundamentals of the AI cycle are described as robust, but semiconductors carry outsized risk capital and are prone to more frequent VaR shocks driven by positioning.

crypto_views: The Senate's failure to advance the CLARITY Act on September 15 has not damaged crypto sentiment, which stayed relatively constructive. Passage this year looks unlikely and hopes shift to 2027.

SEC proposed five-year Innovation Exemption would allow tokenized listed equities to trade longer hours, potentially 24/7, on controlled venues with faster settlement, preserving economic exposure and voting rights. It excludes synthetic tokens and caps venue names and token trading size.

Growing issuer opt-outs from tokenization hurt sentiment for ethereum, with ETH ETF outflows and a weaker ETH futures position proxy, reversing the rise seen right after the September 15 SEC announcement.
The CFTC floated a new market category for leveraged retail crypto on compliant US platforms. It is early stage and implementation is unlikely before 2027.

OCC has granted national trust charters to a growing set of stablecoin issuers and digital asset firms. ICBA has sued the OCC over aspects of the approvals, but charters are hard to unwind once granted.
FASB proposal would let corporate treasuries classify qualifying stablecoins as cash equivalents. Comments are open until November 19.
Bitcoin market price is $83k against a production cost of $88k per JPM's Hayes-style cost-of-production approach.

Elevated long semiconductor exposure among hedge funds and CTAs has likely been largely unwound after the recent declines in semiconductor stocks.
HFRX Equity Hedge has tracked SMH closely since late September, which in corrections can signal forced de-risking by funds with tight risk limits.

geopolitical: Concerns about diversification flows out of US assets resurfaced this year amid tensions over Greenland and after the start of the Middle East conflict.
Diversification fears were first raised after the Liberation Day tariff announcement last year.
Failure of the US Senate to advance the CLARITY Act on September 15 leaves crypto regulation dependent on agency action.
Agency-led crypto rules could be overturned within two years if a Democrat wins the White House.

tension_points.bull_case: Neoclouds are small, with about $30bn of cash flows and $80bn of capex out of $2.2tr and $1.8tr. The tech sector runs a roughly $400bn financing surplus, hyperscalers can absorb the build-out, and surplus firms can fund deficit firms.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising high yield funding costs and higher yields could limit neocloud return headroom, and the timing mismatch between capex and revenues could make the funding model unviable. Stress could spread to other tech companies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Funding concerns spreading beyond neoclouds to other tech companies in a way that buyback deferral and circular financing cannot offset.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity positioning is well below the mid-September peak and elevated long semiconductor exposure has largely unwound, which could limit downside.
tension_points.bear_case: Semiconductors consume about a fifth of global equity risk capital and VaR shocks are becoming more frequent. Hedge fund co-movement with SMH can signal forced de-risking that amplifies drawdowns.

theme_stances.key_argument: Publicly listed neoclouds are a small part of the AI ecosystem and the tech sector runs an aggregate financing surplus, so the AI capex cycle should not be derailed.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not believe that the AI capex cycle will be derailed

theme_stances.key_argument: The rising share of semiconductors in equity markets makes positioning-driven VaR shocks more frequent even when AI fundamentals stay robust.
theme_stances.evidence: semiconductor VaR shocks would become more frequent even if the fundamentals

theme_stances.key_argument: Agency actions help institutional participation but only legislation makes the framework durable, so political and legal risk premia persist.
theme_stances.evidence: elevated political and legal risk premia are likely to persist
